subdivision.heading: General Rule, Considerations and Court Authority

operative_text.controlling:
10.28   In this Division, “party” includes a person filing or
participating in an application or proceeding who is or may be
entitled to or subject to a costs award.

BOOK_A.title: Deﬁnition of “Party”
BOOK_A.commentary:
The court can make a costs order against a non-party who ﬁled a document or participated in
an application, or opposed an application made by the court on its own motion,¹
even if the court
invited certain persons thus to join in.²
An insurer was the real instigator of the litigation and the real one who would have beneﬁtted,
and had been told that it would have to pay costs. Costs were ordered against it when its side lost.³
Even where there are exceptional circumstances (no one to argue the other side), if a tribunal
argues its powers or the merits properly before the Court of Appeal, lack of misconduct does not
immunize it from paying costs if it loses.⁴

footnotes.text: 1985 Sawridge Tr. v. Pub. T’ee. (Stoney v. Twinn) (#9) 2018 ABQB 213, [2018] 7 WWR 411 (¶’s 17, 18), revd 2019 ABCA 244, Edm 1803 0076 AC (citing this book) ; Dezotell Hldg. v. St. -Jean (#2) 2019 ABQB 476, 99 Alta LR(6th) 368 (¶’s 9-16) (participated in motion and appeal, and one ﬁled evidence and a brief).
Wang v. Alta.2022 ABCA 79, Calg 2101 0003 AC (Mar 4) (¶’s 19-23) (vexatious litigant process joined with parties affected).
Ernst & Young v. Cent. Guar. Tr.2010 ABQB 26, 479 AR 202 (¶’s 88-113).
Univ. of Calg. v. J. R.2015 ABCA 118, 382 DLR(4th) 299 (¶’s 52-56).

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.10-42 (line 2049) to p.10-43 (line 2083): title (line 2049; the division headings 'DIVISION 2 / RECOVERABLE COSTS OF LITIGATION / Subdivision 1 / General Rule, Considerations and Court Authority' are lines 2045-2048 above it and belong to the 10.27 range), rule text (lines 2050-2052), the p.10-42 footnote block (line 2054 ff., holding the 10.27 note's fns 1-5), the page marker 10-43 (line 2064), the Information Note (lines 2066-2070), Related Provisions (lines 2072-2073: 'Appendix - "party"; 10.50 (costs payable by lawyer)') and the note (lines 2075-2083) with its footnotes: p.10-43 fns 1-4 (block after the text of 10.29(1), line 2102 ff.) = 4. Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.28 (EXACT_MATCH, no differences). The Information Note ('Party is defined in the Appendix [Definitions] as a party to an action. There are other Court proceedings that are not "actions" and so the definition of party is expanded to allow a costs award against anyone participating in an application or proceeding that is not an action started by statement of claim or originating application.') is not in the official text (which prints no information notes) and ends with a stray backtick '`' (extraction); its content agrees with the Appendix definition of 'party' ('a party to an action; in Part 10, Division 2 ... an extended meaning'). The Related Provisions labels: 'Appendix - "party"' lands on the Appendix definition; '10.50 (costs payable by lawyer)' is a label for official 10.50 ('Costs imposed on lawyer'), whose Book A Related Provisions point back to '10.28 ("party")'. The note is case-law summary, not the rule: costs against a non-party who filed a document or participated (fn 1 1985 Sawridge Tr. v. Pub. T'ee. (Stoney v. Twinn) (#9) 2018 ABQB 213, revd 2019 ABCA 244 '(citing this book)'; Dezotell Hldg. v. St.-Jean (#2) 2019 ABQB 476, paras 9-16); persons the court invited to join (fn 2 Wang v. Alta. 2022 ABCA 79, paras 19-23); the insurer that instigated the litigation (fn 3 Ernst & Young v. Cent. Guar. Tr. 2010 ABQB 26, paras 88-113); a tribunal that argues its powers or the merits (fn 4 Univ. of Calg. v. J. R. 2015 ABCA 118, paras 52-56; Book B's 10.31 commentary has the Workers' Compensation Board as a party under 10.28, Justice Lee, 2011 ABQB 367). Pointers into this rule from other Book A passages: the 10.34 Related Provisions cite '10.28(2)' (no such subrule) and the 9.14 Related Provisions label 10.28 '(costs awards after trial)' (the official title is 'Definition of "party"'); see-also. supra/infra: no supra or infra is used in this note. Printed as is: 'St. -Jean' (a space before the hyphen), 'Cent. Guar. Tr.2010 ABQB 26'.

information_notes.text:
Party is defined in the Appendix [Definitions] as a party to an action. There are other Court
proceedings that are not “actions” and so the definition of party is expanded to allow a costs
award against anyone participating in an application or proceeding that is not an action
started by statement of claim or originating application. `
